text:
Mina: heads-up — I'm opening a terraform change to switch our gpu spot fleets to capacity-optimized + add an interruption handler in the launch template user_data. hoping to cut costs without increasing OOM risk.

Charlie: nice. can you paste the snippet you're planning? curious about the handler approach.

Mina: sure. leaning on the instance metadata termination-time URL and a tiny SSM run command to drain pods. idea: user_data writes a small systemd service that watches for the 2-minute shutdown notice and calls our drain script. snippet:```hcl
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_spot_lt" {
  name_prefix = "redwood-gpu-spot-" 
  lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }
  instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge" # will change to mixed later
  user_data = base64encode(<<-EOF
#!/bin/bash
cat > /usr/local/bin/spot-interrupt-handler.sh << 'EOL'
#!/bin/bash
if [ -f /var/run/spot-interrupt.lock ]; then exit 0; fi
# check metadata for termination time
TERM_TIME=$(curl -s -m 1 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/instance-action || true)
if [ -n "$TERM_TIME" ]; then
  /usr/local/bin/drain-node.sh
fi
EOL
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/spot-interrupt-handler.sh
systemctl enable --now spot-interrupt-handler.service
EOF
  )
}
```

Raj: watcher approach is OK but two notes: 1) metadata path can differ by region and older AMIs, test in staging AMI; 2) AWS sometimes sends rebalance before the 2-min notice — consider subscribing to the instance rebalance signal (EC2:RebalanceRecommendation) via CloudWatch Events -> SNS -> SQS so our autoscaler can preemptively reprovision.

Ashley: also we should switch allocation_strategy to "capacity-optimized" in the ASG/fleet. low-price was giving us too many interruptions in eu-west last month. cost impact chart I ran shows ~18% token cost reduction with capacity-optimized + mixed instance types.

Mina: good call. plan in the TF change: move to mixed_instances_policy with weights; prefer cheaper A100 alternatives where perf matches (g4dn -> g5?), and tag everything with env, team, pool, and ami-hash for quicker rollbacks. draft:```hcl
mixed_instances_policy {
  instances_distribution {
    on_demand_allocation_strategy = "prioritized"
    spot_allocation_strategy = "capacity-optimized"
    spot_instance_pools = 6
  }
  launch_template {
    launch_template_specification { launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.gpu_spot_lt.id }
    overrides = [
      { instance_type = "g5.12xlarge" , weighted_capacity = 1 },
      { instance_type = "g5.24xlarge" , weighted_capacity = 2 },
      { instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge" , weighted_capacity = 4 }
    ]
  }
}
```

Charlie: make sure to put explicit cpu/memory limits in the kube node labels and taints so scheduler doesn't pack too many pods on cheaper smaller instances. otherwise we end up with noisy-neighbor tails.

Mina: yep — adding kubelet extra-args via user_data to set reserved resources. also adding an AMI bake pipeline change: include the metadata client and our drain script in the image so user_data is minimal. will test AMI in staging eu-west-1 and us-west-2.

Raj: about rollout: please do canary by AZ and limit replace percentage to 10% per hour. and add a tf var toggle to flip back to on-demand for the affected ASG quickly.

Mina: putting that in the PR description. CI bot will run the plan: @ci-bot please run plan on the eng-infra/gpu-fleet module after I push. PR will include:
- change allocation strategy to capacity-optimized
- add mixed_instances_policy overrides
- user_data change to interruption handler service (with AMI baked alternative)
- tags: {Env,Team,Pool,AMI}
- rollout constraints: canary by az, max 10% replace/hour, tf var for quick revert

ci-bot: CI plan queued for run id 8923. will post plan output here when complete.

Ashley: also add a network note — we hit ENI limit on smaller instances in ap-northeast-1 before. ensure max_enis and ip_per_eni are compatible across chosen instance types. add a preflight check in the pipeline.

Mina: thanks — adding preflight script to verify ENI/cidr limits per instance type and region.

Charlie: sounds solid. after canary, let's monitor pod eviction metrics and p95 latency. set a regression alert for >3% failure or 200ms tail increase.

Mina: agreed. I'll open the PR now and add the monitoring playbook. if anyone wants to review the TF and user_data, ping me. :thumbsup:
